chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Abu al-Subbah, who said:

By Allah, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Indeed, Allah taught His Prophet the Tanzil (exoteric revelation) and the Ta'wil (esoteric interpretation), so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him).'
He said, 'And Allah taught us.' Then he said, 'Whatever you do or swear an oath upon for the sake of Taqiyyah (dissimulation/prudence), you are in ease (exempt) from it.'

key_terms.التَّنْزِيل: Exoteric revelation or the literal text of the Quran
key_terms.تَقِيَّة: Prudent dissimulation or concealment of faith to avoid harm
key_terms.فِي سَعَةٍ: In ease or exemption, indicating no penalty for the oath
key_terms.والتَّأْوِيل: Esoteric interpretation or inner meaning of revelation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on oaths taken for Taqiyyah in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq underscores the dual nature of divine revelation, distinguishing between the exoteric text (Tanzil) and its esoteric interpretation (Ta'wil), which was transmitted through the Prophet to Ali and subsequently to the Imams. It provides a specific jurisprudential ruling that oaths sworn for the sake of Taqiyyah are released from their binding force, reflecting the practical flexibility granted to Shia believers in times of danger or concealment.
